about: Campaign Mode's four challengers (docs/CAMPAIGN-MODE.md section 2; owner, Oct 29). Every name is invented. Numbers are starting values for playtests: cash in C$, donor and channels are multipliers (1 = average), debate is 0 to 3 per style, places are starting points of lean.

candidates.name: Preston Vale Goldcrest III
candidates.title: The Disruptor
candidates.slogan: Let's run this city like a business. Mine.
candidates.bio: Inherited a parking-garage empire and calls himself self-made. Founder of Goldcrest Holdings: eleven luxury towers, a members-only kombucha bar and $QUEENS, a crypto coin that failed. Has never ridden the subway, but once funded a documentary about it.

issues.title: Towers everywhere
issues.line: Rezone Astoria for luxury high-rises. Supply! Eventually, trickling down!

issues.title: The private city
issues.line: A premium Concierge Lane, private patrols and VIP lines at the motor vehicles office.

issues.title: The East River gondola
issues.line: His signature project. C$40 a ride.

candidates.satire: Billionaires who think buying something means fixing it.

lines.text: Goldcrest asked a Woodside crowd who still takes the bus. Several people raised their hands. -1.
Goldcrest tipped a deli worker C$500 on camera. Gross, but it played. +1.
Goldcrest called the 7 train "rustic." The 7 train did not take it well. -1.

candidates.name: Dr. Ingrid Castellano
candidates.title: The Professor
candidates.slogan: I've done the math. You're welcome.
candidates.bio: Former professor of urban systems at St. Johnsons University. Wrote a 600-page report on the 7 train that nobody at City Hall read, so she's running to read it to them. Methodical, dry, always carries a chart. Her students loved her; her colleagues feared her office hours.

issues.title: Transit that runs
issues.line: Signal upgrades for the 7, bus lanes, and arrival times that don't lie.

issues.title: Flood-proof Queens
issues.line: Green roofs, storm drains and a waterfront seawall before the next big storm.

issues.title: Schools and libraries
issues.line: Longer library hours, free tutoring, smaller classes.

issues.title: Open books
issues.line: A public site for every city dollar, with a budget she audits herself.

candidates.satire: The expert who is right and can't make anyone care.
candidates.refuseLine: "I won't put my name on a number I made up." Talk her round? It'll cost the team's morale.

lines.text: Castellano gave a 40-minute answer at a Sunnyside town hall. Half the room left. The other half joined. 0.
Castellano's flood chart went viral with students. +1.
Castellano corrected a voter's math at a rally. Correctly. -1.

candidates.name: Frankie "The Hammer" Kowalczyk
candidates.title: The Organizer
candidates.slogan: This city runs on people. Pay 'em.
candidates.bio: Ran Local 117 of the city's transit workers for 22 years, and he has a knee that "remembers the strike of '09." Loud, warm, impossible to bully. Knows every bodega owner in Woodside by first name and brings a thermos to every meeting. Retired, got bored in three weeks, started a campaign.

issues.title: Rent
issues.line: Caps on rent hikes, a tenant hotline someone answers, and boilers that work.

issues.title: Wages
issues.line: A raise for city workers, delivery riders and home aides. No more unpaid overtime.

issues.title: Keep the neighborhood
issues.line: Protect the bodegas and small shops from the towers.

issues.title: Safety the old way
issues.line: Crossing guards, streetlights and night buses.

candidates.satire: The lovable old-school fighter who can't stand change.
candidates.refuseLine: "Frankie don't buy people. Frankie organizes 'em." Talk him round? It'll cost the team's morale.

lines.text: Frankie argued with a heckler in Jackson Heights and won. The clip is everywhere. +1.
Frankie asked a reporter what a "hashtag" is, live. -1.
Frankie's knee predicted rain. It rained. Woodside is impressed. +1.

candidates.name: Kaylee Starr
candidates.title: The Influencer
candidates.bio: 2.3 million followers, a sponsored tea, and a "Mayor era" announced in a get-ready-with-me video. Decided to run when City Hall didn't repost her. Surprisingly good at it.

issues.title: Nightlife
issues.line: Clubs open until 6am, content zones in every park, a ring-light at every subway stop.

issues.title: The 2am Slice Protection Act
issues.line: Pizza places stay open late. Forever.

candidates.satire: Fame as a qualification, which is Clout City's whole premise.

lines.text: Kaylee went live from the campaign office and showed the strategy whiteboard. -1.
Kaylee's slice-shop tour got 4 million views. +2.
Kaylee called the subway "a vibe, honestly." Commuters disagree. -1.
